2017_112_090517spmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for a Troy Board of Education special meeting held at 5:45 PM on September 5, 2017 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. Three items carry the meeting: ratification of a successor Letter of Understanding with the International Academy teachers running July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2022; a $681,737.50 furniture purchase for secondary math classrooms through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program, charged to the 2016 Capital Projects Fund; and a waived first reading plus second-reading adoption of revised policies 2000.07 Health and Safety, 5000.03 Purchasing, and either 0000.02 Board of Education or 4000.01 Administrative Staff and Organization.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education special meeting, September 5, 2017, 5:45 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication; Personnel; Business; Other; Adjournment. The packet notes that when school is in session, meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**3.A. Personnel — International Academy Letter of Understanding**
Ratification of a successor Letter of Understanding with the teachers at the International Academy, a consortium high school program. The tentative agreement was reached March 9, 2017, concluded May 31, 2017, and ratified by the IA teachers June 8, 2017; the term is July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2022. Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent/Employee Services, and Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal/IA East, represented Troy on the bargaining team; Harris and Christine Barnett (Bloomfield Hills) signed as chief negotiators, with Grat Dalton signing as Executive Director. Signature pages are held in the Human Resources Office of Bloomfield Hills Schools.

Negotiated changes include a five-year term; IA administration rather than the Joint Steering Committee determining applicant qualifications; termination language now referencing the home district's policies and procedures and applicable law, reflecting 2011 changes to the Public Employment Relations Act that made discipline and discharge a prohibited subject of bargaining; a new tri-campus club committee for supplemental-activity categories; a new Department Chairs article; new teaching-schedule language on preparation periods; and a Standing Committee of up to five teacher and up to five administration representatives.

**Stipends and supplemental pay**
The former two-tier stipend (under five years / five or more years of experience) is replaced by a single stipend per district, effective July 1, 2017, rising $50.00 at each Base step:

| District | BASE | Base +4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avondale, Berkley, Clawson, Waterford, West Bloomfield | $3,600.00 | $3,800.00 |
| Huron Valley | $3,400.00 | $3,600.00 |
| Birmingham | $3,050.00 | $3,250.00 |
| Lake Orion, Royal Oak, Troy | $2,850.00 | $3,050.00 |
| Rochester | $2,700.00 | $2,900.00 |
| Bloomfield Hills | $2,350.00 | $2,550.00 |

Teachers previously in the 5+ year range receive a one-time 2017-18 bonus: $143.00 for Troy, Lake Orion and Royal Oak; $121.00 Huron Valley; $119.00 Birmingham; $117.00 Rochester; $115.00 Bloomfield Hills; $97.00 for Avondale, Berkley, Clawson, Waterford and West Bloomfield. Supplemental pay rates are Category I $866, Category II $1190, Category III $1570, with department-chair remuneration for all campuses capped at $10,990 over the contract term. Enrichment and orientation activities, substituting for another Academy teacher, and out-of-day parent/teacher conferences pay $25 per hour; the further math class carries a $3500.00 annual stipend.

**4.A. Business — Furniture Purchase, Secondary Math Classrooms**
Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, led a project team with Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and building administrators and staff to evaluate furniture needs in secondary math classrooms. The resolution approves $681,737.50 through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The accompanying presentation lists installation at $49,580.00 and an estimated rebate of $27,000 (4%), and allocates the package by building: Troy High School $168,450.06, Athens High School $145,148.20, Boulan Middle School $70,558.46, Larson Middle School $68,773.68, Baker Middle School $66,680.00, Smith Middle School $59,067.80, IA East $30,621.00 and TCCHS $22,858.30.

**5. Other — Policies**
Under policy 1000.03, the Board is asked to waive a first reading and then take a second reading and adopt revised policies 2000.07 Health and Safety, 5000.03 Purchasing, and either 0000.02 Board of Education or 4000.01 Administrative Staff and Organization. The packet carries both variants because the choice depends on which policy is amended to strike the negotiating-team language. Revised 2000.07 adds language complying with Michigan law prohibiting seclusion and restraint except for emergency seclusion and emergency physical restraint in the manner permitted by law.

Agenda packet for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, September 5, 2017 at 5:45 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. The agenda lists: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel — Consideration: IA Contract Addendum; 4. Business — Consideration: Furniture Purchase, Secondary Math Classrooms; 5. Other — Consideration: Waive the First Reading of Policies 0000.02/4000.01, 5000.03 and 2000.07, and Consideration: Second Reading and Adoption of Revised Board Policies; 6. Adjournment. The cover page notes meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and can be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Richard Machesky, Ed.D. is Superintendent of Schools.

**Personnel: successor Letter of Understanding, International Academy teachers.** The Board is asked to ratify and adopt the tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the International Academy teachers for the period July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2022. The agreement was reached March 9, 2017 but not concluded until May 31, 2017, and the International Academy teachers ratified it June 8, 2017. Mr. Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent/Employee Services, and Mr. Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal/IA East, represented the Troy School District on the bargaining team. The signature page names Grat Dalton, Executive Director; Christine Barnett, Chief Negotiator; and Jordan Harris, Chief Negotiator, with actual signature pages on file in the Human Resources Office of Bloomfield Hills Schools.

The International Academy is a consortium of public school districts operating a grade nine through twelve school-of-choice program at several campuses. The participating districts are Avondale, Berkley, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Clawson, Huron Valley, Lake Orion, Rochester, Royal Oak, Troy, Waterford and West Bloomfield. The administrative team representing the districts: Lynne Gibson (principal of the IA), Sarah Fairman (IB Coordinator), Christopher Smith (associate principal, IA Central), Ryan Brinks (associate principal, IA East), Ryan Parrott (associate principal, IA West), Jordan Harris (Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, Troy) and Christine Barnett (Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources and Labor Relations, Bloomfield Hills). The teacher team: Dave McGuire (IA-East), Jeff DeMoss (IA-East), Kayla McCabe (IA-Okma) and Kelly Paterson (IA-East). Teachers assigned to the Academy remain employees of their home district; tenure is with the home district.

Article-by-article changes described in the cover memo: Article 1 sets a five-year term. Article 2(b) clarifies that the IA administration, not the Joint Steering Committee, determines applicant qualifications. Article 2(d) replaces reference to the home district's collective bargaining agreement and the Michigan Teachers' Tenure Act with the "home district's policies and procedures and applicable law," because 2011 changes to the Public Employment Relations Act made decisions on discipline or discharge of teachers a prohibited subject of bargaining. Article 4 revises the process for approving paid clubs and organizations to include a tri-campus club committee of teachers and administrators, which recommends a category to Administration; the administration approves and designates the category within ten school days. Article 5 is new and names Department Chairs for literature, history, math, theory of knowledge, French/German, Spanish, chemistry, physics, biology, economics, art, music, physical education/health and counseling, paid at Category III. New Article 9(c) provides that every effort will be made to give preparation periods on C Day, Interdisciplinary Day and outside evaluation days, though not every teacher will have one. New Article 9(d) provides that non-music teachers assigned five or more preparations per semester will receive an extra planning period for at least one semester where possible, or compensation of 1/16 of salary for the additional instruction block. Article 11(g) changes Standing Committee representation from "representatives of the current negotiation team" to up to five teacher and up to five administration representatives, because not all current negotiators will be available across the five-year term.

**Wages, stipends and supplemental pay.** Teachers are paid for required days according to their home district's step and salary track. Appendix A replaces the previous two-tier stipend (fewer than five years of experience versus five or more) with one stipend per district beginning July 1, 2017, increasing $50.00 at each Base step: Avondale, Berkley, Clawson, Waterford and West Bloomfield $3,600.00 BASE rising to $3,800.00 at Base +4; Huron Valley $3,400.00 to $3,600.00; Birmingham $3,050.00 to $3,250.00; Lake Orion, Royal Oak and Troy $2,850.00 to $3,050.00; Rochester $2,700.00 to $2,900.00; Bloomfield Hills $2,350.00 to $2,550.00. All teachers begin at the BASE stipend in 2017-18; from 2018-19 each returning IA teacher moves to Base +1 and then to the next level annually until reaching Base +4. Part-time teachers are prorated by FTE. Teachers who had been in the 5+ year range under the 2014-2017 Letter of Understanding receive a one-time 2017-18 bonus of $150 less the increase in their stipend: $143.00 for Lake Orion, Royal Oak and Troy; $121.00 Huron Valley; $119.00 Birmingham; $117.00 Rochester; $115.00 Bloomfield Hills; and $97.00 for Avondale, Berkley, Clawson, Waterford and West Bloomfield. The memo's worked example is a Berkley 5+ year teacher whose current longer year and longer day stipend is $3547, against a new base of $3600, leaving $53 and a stipend bonus of $97.

The superseded Appendix A-1 table (fewer than five years) shows a $118.08 difference rate and a $1200.00 longer-day allocation, running from 182 days in the home district at $1180.80 and $2380.80 total additional compensation down to 192 days at $0.00 and $1200.00. The five-years-experience table shows a $175.90 rate and $1787.50 allocation, from $1759.00 and $3546.50 at 182 days to $0.00 and $1787.50 at 192 days; 182 days is the minimum used in the calculation.

Appendix B sets supplemental pay at Category I $866, Category II $1190 and Category III $1570. Category I covers class sponsors for 9th and 10th grades, the Mentor/Mentee Committee Chair and IA-mission-related clubs; Category II covers the 11th grade class sponsor, honor societies, coordinators (Passport, Product Team, buildOn, Theory of Knowledge, School Improvement, Student Leadership, Extended Essay), assistant coaches and the Honors Convocation counselor duty; Category III covers the 12th grade class sponsor, department chairs, the Extended Essay Coordinator, coaches for competitive teams, the Student Leadership Advisor, Yearbook Advisor, graduation planning and the Directors of Fine Arts. Total remuneration for department heads across all campuses is capped at $10,990 during the term of the contract. A club or organization requires a minimum of ten students and must meet the equivalent of at least eighty minutes per month.

Other compensation terms: enrichment and orientation activities pay $25 per hour, with a maximum of eight hours per day (a seven hour and fifty minute day is paid as eight), a maximum of forty hours per activity, and principal discretion to designate up to six activities per year compensated up to 64 hours; travel time is capped at four hours. Substituting for another Academy teacher pays $25 per hour, as do parent/teacher conferences held outside the regular school day. The teacher assigned to the further math class receives a stipend of $3500.00 per school year.

**Work year and schedule.** Teachers work 192 days including 190 student days, with 190 instructional days plus enrichment/orientation days. Each teacher receives one paid discretionary day, non-cumulative, scheduled first-come first-served with no more than ten percent of staff off on any one day and scheduling completed by April 15. The International Academy provides a minimum of 30 professional development hours: 24 specified in the calendars and 6 more scheduled by November 1 each year, all completed by June 1, with pay docked one hour for each hour missed. The normal daily teacher schedule is seven hours and fifty minutes with 270 minutes of instructional time; in an eight-block schedule over two days a full-time teacher has six instructional blocks, and over a two-week period the workweek averages 250 minutes of preparation time per week. Lunch is a daily thirty-minute duty-free period, and homeroom/passport is not intended to exceed an average of forty minutes bi-weekly. Music teachers teach a Block E course and are assigned five rather than six instructional blocks for the corresponding period, or are compensated 1/16 of salary.

**Grievance procedure.** A grievance must be presented in writing to the IA principal within fifteen working days of the occurrence or of the grievant becoming aware of it; the principal schedules a meeting within five work days and responds in writing within five work days. Step Two goes to the Joint Steering Committee's Grievance Committee within ten work days; that committee has three representatives from the constituent districts, one from the grievant's home district, meets within ten work days and responds within five. Step Three is binding arbitration, which only the Association may invoke, filed within twenty work days under American Arbitration Association rules, with the losing party paying the arbitrator's fees and expenses. The arbitrator has no authority to alter, amend, add to or subtract from the agreement.

**Business: furniture purchase for secondary math classrooms.** Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, led a project team with Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and building administrators and staff to evaluate the use and needs for furniture in secondary math classrooms. The suggested resolution approves the bid for furniture for secondary math classrooms in the amount of $681,737.50 through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The attached "The Learning Environment" presentation, which opens with a Franklin D. Roosevelt quotation, states a Total Investment of $681,737.50, installation of $49,580.00 and an estimated rebate of $27,000 (4%), with pricing including professionally coordinated delivery and installation during normal business hours and project management. Building allocations are Troy High School $168,450.06, Athens High School $145,148.20, Baker Middle School $66,680.00, Boulan Middle School $70,558.46, Smith Middle School $59,067.80, Larson Middle School $68,773.68, IA East $30,621.00 and TCCHS $22,858.30. The package selection tables list Package A totalling 2 (Smith 1, Boulan 1); Package B totalling 18 (Smith 3, Larson 1, IA East 1, Boulan 5, Athens 3, Troy HS 5); Package C totalling 1 (Smith 1); Package D totalling 9 (Athens 1, Troy HS 8); Package E totalling 6 (Smith 1, Larson 3, Baker 2); Package F totalling 17 (Larson 1, IA East 2, Boulan 1, Athens 8, Baker 1, Troy HS 4); Package G totalling 4 (Smith 1, Athens 1, Baker 2); and Package H totalling 5 (Larson 1, Athens 2, Baker 2).

**Other: policy readings.** Under policy 1000.03, Adoption or Amendment of Bylaws and Policies, the Board may by majority vote waive a first reading and proceed to act on a revision or new policy. The packet carries two alternative versions of both the waiver and the adoption resolution: one naming policies 0000.02 Board of Education, 5000.03 Purchasing and 2000.07 Health and Safety, to be used if 0000.02 is changed to strike language stating that the Board approves the negotiating team; the other naming 4000.01 Administrative Staff and Organization, 5000.03 Purchasing and 2000.07 Health and Safety, to be used if 4000.01 is changed to strike language stating that the superintendent appoints the negotiating team. Revised policy 2000.07 Health and Safety includes new language to comply with Michigan law prohibiting seclusion and restraint, except for emergency seclusion and emergency physical restraint in the manner permitted by law.
